A leukotriene-dependent increase in airway IL-33 is supported in dust-mite-primed Ptges-null mice. The human route, cellular receptor and intervening inflammatory effects are not established by this experiment.
Available extracellular IL-33 can engage ST2. Translation from greater tissue abundance to increased released, active ligand remains inferred in human AERD.
IL-33 blockade and soluble ST2-Fc reduce mast-cell-associated mediator release in the mouse model. Human cellular mediation remains an extrapolation.
IL-33 can activate type 2 innate lymphoid and T-helper cells; its necessary contribution in individual human AERD patients is unresolved.
TSLP stimulation promotes a mediator-producing mast-cell state in human culture experiments.
TSLP can stimulate type 2 lymphoid cells in the broader alarmin network.
Activated mast cells contribute PGD2, although they are not its exclusive source.
Activated mast cells contribute cysteinyl leukotrienes; anti-IgE stimulation of cultured AERD donor cells increases their release.
PGD2 promotes bronchoconstriction, including through thromboxane-prostanoid receptor signaling; model antagonist data do not establish PGD2 as the sole ligand.
PGD2 can recruit and activate type 2 lymphoid cells through CRTH2; this route is not proven to dominate chronic polyp disease.
Type 2 lymphoid cytokine production supplies IL-5.
Type 2 lymphoid cytokines supply IL-13 and related IL-4R-alpha ligands; mast cells are an additional IL-13 source.
IL-5 supports the eosinophilic compartment through production and survival pathways; recruitment also depends on chemotactic signals.

IL-4R-alpha signaling contributes to the inflammatory process sustaining polyps; receptor blockade improves polyp burden, but the necessary intermediate cells and remodeling steps are incompletely resolved.
Blocking this receptor pathway improves lower-airway disease in selected AERD cohorts; multiple cellular intermediates may contribute.
Smooth-muscle contraction contributes to the bronchospastic component of the exposure-related reaction; upper-airway reactions can occur without bronchospasm.
Airway narrowing can produce expiratory wheeze.
Bronchomotor narrowing contributes to breathlessness during lower-airway reactions.
Mediator-associated edema contributes to congestion during acute reactions; chronic obstruction has additional causes.

nodes.description: A specialist option for confirmed AERD with persistent symptoms, recurrent polyps or a separate need for aspirin. Benefits vary by patient and regimen: one 34-person randomized trial reported symptom/medication benefit, whereas a 2025 trial randomizing 26 successfully desensitized participants found no significant between-group difference in SNOT-22, asthma-control or polyp scores over 11 months. That trial used 125 mg daily initially then 250 mg and does not exclude benefit from other regimens. Screen for uncontrolled asthma, ulcer/bleeding risk, pregnancy and ability to adhere. Daily maintenance is needed; more than two missed days requires reassessment before unsupervised resumption.

nodes.description: An IL-4R-alpha blocker used in eligible uncontrolled asthma/CRSwNP. In an open-label AERD cohort, 7 of 30 tolerated the highest aspirin challenge dose after six months and another 10 tolerated higher doses; this was not universal tolerance or a placebo-controlled comparison. A nested 11-person 2026 mechanistic analysis found reduced nasal type 2 responses without a cytokine pattern reliably distinguishing tolerance; transcriptional associations do not establish mediation. evidence.snippet: The respiratory reactions to COX-1 inhibitors involve the acute onset of nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, sneezing, nasal pruritus, ocular chemosis, and/or bronchospasm within 30 min to 3 h of exposure.

nodes.description: Bilateral polyps are characteristic and may recur after surgery. Early or partial presentations can precede the full triad.

evidence.snippet: N-ERD is characterized by the triad of asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), and respiratory reactions to cyclooxygenase (COX)-1 inhibitors.

nodes.description: Anti-IgE treatment may be selected under the applicable asthma/CRSwNP indication. A 16-person atopic AERD crossover trial reduced challenge-associated urinary LTE4 and allowed 10 participants to tolerate the highest tested aspirin dose after three months. Six still reacted; generalization to nonatopic or uncontrolled severe disease is limited. Biomarker reductions imply reduced mediator activity but do not directly identify the responsible airway cell population.

evidence.reference_title: Omalizumab for Aspirin Hypersensitivity and Leukotriene Overproduction in Aspirin-exacerbated Respiratory Disease. A Randomized Controlled Trial.
evidence.snippet: Ten of 16 patients (62.5%) developed oral aspirin tolerance up to cumulative doses of 930 mg in the omalizumab phase

evidence.snippet: The mechanisms by which IgE can induce a chronically activated mast cell population, and the antigen specificity of the locally produced IgE remain to be determined.

nodes.description: Aspirin and other strong COX-1 inhibitors suppress cyclooxygenase activity. This acute pharmacologic exposure triggers reactions in a susceptible airway; it does not explain the acquired chronic asthma and sinonasal disease.

evidence.reference_title: Updating the classification and routine diagnosis of NSAID hypersensitivity reactions: A WAO Statement.
evidence.snippet: Inhibition of COX-1 activity in patients with N-ERD further reduces the “braking” effects of PGE2/EP2 on mast cells and 5-LO activity, which increases the release of cysLTs in urine and airway fluids, precipitating respiratory symptoms.

nodes.description: A study of 12 aspirin-sensitive and 10 non-sensitive rhinosinusitis polyps found a lower fraction of inflammatory cells expressing EP2. Global mucosal EP2 staining was increased, largely in epithelial/goblet cells. Abundance is distinguished from a direct functional-response assay.

evidence.reference_title: Aspirin-sensitive rhinosinusitis is associated with reduced E-prostanoid 2 receptor expression on nasal mucosal inflammatory cells.
evidence.snippet: the percentages of neutrophils, mast cells, eosinophils, and T cells expressing EP(2), but not EP(1), EP(3), or EP(4), were significantly reduced (P < or = .04) in the aspirin-sensitive compared with nonaspirin-sensitive patients

nodes.description: Loss of some PGE2-mediated inhibition permits greater mediator synthesis and cellular activation. This is a context-dependent signaling defect: PGE2 still suppressed anti-IgE-induced cysteinyl leukotriene release in cultured blood-progenitor-derived mast cells from AERD donors. Inhaled PGE2 also protected against aspirin challenge in a small crossover study.

evidence.reference_title: Updates on immune mechanisms in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease.
evidence.snippet: PGE2 stabilizes and prevents the activation of mast cells (2) and group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s)(3), and prevents the formation of cysLTs by inhibiting the translocation of 5-lipoxygenase (5-LO) (4).

evidence.reference_title: PGE suppresses excessive anti-IgE induced cysteinyl leucotrienes production in mast cells of patients with aspirin exacerbated respiratory disease.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, PGE(2) suppressed only anti-IgE induced cys-LTs release from mast cells of AERD patients.

evidence.reference_title: Inhaled PGE2 prevents aspirin-induced bronchoconstriction and urinary LTE4 excretion in aspirin-sensitive asthma.
evidence.snippet: Inhaled PGE2 provided almost complete protection in all patients.

nodes.description: Reduced production and/or increased catabolism lowers protective PGE2 availability in respiratory tissues. Chronic COX-2/mPGES-1 abnormalities and acute COX-1 inhibition are distinct contributors; neither complete PGE2 absence nor a single initiating lesion is established.

animal_models.description: Loss of mPGES-1 impairs inducible PGE2 synthesis.

evidence.snippet: Several studies link AERD to diminished production (or increased catabolism) of PGE2 in the respiratory tract

nodes.description: A TSLP-blocking option for patients meeting a relevant severe-asthma indication. In the 52-week NAVIGATOR analysis, the post hoc subgroup with a history of aspirin or NSAID sensitivity had an estimated 83% lower annualized exacerbation rate than placebo (95% CI 66–91). This subgroup is distinct from the smaller recorded AERD/N-ERD/Samter triad subgroup. No formal hypothesis testing or between-biologic comparison was performed; the result does not establish aspirin tolerance or superiority for challenge-confirmed AERD.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of Tezepelumab in Patients with Severe, Uncontrolled Asthma Across Multiple Clinically Relevant Subgroups in the NAVIGATOR Study.
evidence.snippet: Reductions with tezepelumab compared with placebo in patients with asthma‑related comorbidities ranged from 58% (95% CI: 47, 67) in patients with rhinitis to 83% (95% CI: 66, 91) in patients with aspirin or NSAID sensitivity

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of Tezepelumab in Patients with Severe, Uncontrolled Asthma Across Multiple Clinically Relevant Subgroups in the NAVIGATOR Study.
evidence.snippet: No formal hypothesis testing was performed to compare tezepelumab with placebo or to compare effects between the subgroups investigated.

nodes.description: Use topical anti-inflammatory sinonasal therapy and saline irrigation as part of chronic rhinosinusitis care, including after surgery when appropriate. Delivery and adherence matter; extensive polyps may limit topical penetration.

nodes.description: Type 2 lymphoid cells, including ILC2s and Th2 cells, contribute cytokines to the airway network. Challenge-associated redistribution of ILC2s is observed in humans, whereas depletion-based necessity was tested in mice.

nodes.description: A 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor that reduces leukotriene production. It is a selected adjunct for persistent airway symptoms and can attenuate reactions; its use requires attention to drug-specific contraindications, interactions and monitoring.

evidence.snippet: Treatment with zileuton, which inhibits 5-LO and decreases production of leukotrienes, attenuates the sinonasal symptoms (16), lung function changes (17), and gastrointestinal and cutaneous symptoms that occur during aspirin-induced reactions in AERD.
